record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Prove the existence of nonsingular asymptotically flat static spherically symmetric solutions of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills (EYM) equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime with gauge group SU(2): the coupled system consisting of Einstein's field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}$, where $T_{\mu\nu}$ is the stress-energy tensor of a Yang-Mills connection $A$ with curvature $F$, together with the Yang-Mills equations $D^\mu F_{\mu\nu} = 0$ for $A$ on the resulting spacetime. Seek static, spherically symmetric solutions; with the standard ansatz, the metric takes the form
$$ ds^2 = -A(r) C(r)^2\, dt^2 + A(r)^{-1}\, dr^2 + r^2 (d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\, d\phi^2), $$
and the Yang-Mills connection is given by a single real "magnetic" potential $w(r)$. The reduced equations are
$$ r A' = 1 - A - \frac{(1-w^2)^2}{r^2} - 2 A (w')^2,\qquad r^2 A w'' + \big(r(1-A) - \tfrac{(1-w^2)^2}{r}\big) w' + w(1-w^2) = 0, $$
together with an ODE for $C$. Prove the existence of a globally defined, nonsingular (i.e. $A(r) > 0$ for all $r \ge 0$ with $A(0)=1$ and $w(0)=\pm 1$), asymptotically flat (i.e. $A(r) \to 1$, $C(r) \to 1$, $w(r) \to \pm 1$ as $r \to \infty$ with finite ADM mass) solution $(A, C, w)$ on $[0,\infty)$. Equivalently, establish the existence of static spherically symmetric soliton (particle-like) solutions of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of nonsingular, asymptotically flat, static, spherically symmetric soliton solutions of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations (the Bartnik–McKinnon solutions, originally found numerically) was rigorously proved by Smoller, Wasserman, Yau, and McLeod in the early 1990s in "Smooth Static Solutions of the Einstein/Yang-Mills Equations" (Comm. Math. Phys., 1991/1993), with further work establishing a countable family parametrized by the number of zeros of $w$. The problem is therefore solved.

status_evidence.title: Smooth static solutions of the Einstein/Yang-Mills equations
status_evidence.snippet: Smoller, Wasserman, Yau and McLeod prove existence of a globally defined smooth static solution to the SU(2) Einstein/Yang-Mills equations with asymptotically flat metric and finite total mass.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of nonsingular asymptotically flat static spherically symmetric EYM solitons is rigorously proven.

status_evidence.title: Smooth static solutions of the Einstein-Yang/Mills equation (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous proof of existence of smooth static solutions to the Einstein-Yang/Mills equations.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms existence proof of EYM solitons.

status_evidence.title: Static spherically symmetric solutions of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations
status_evidence.snippet: Family of regular solutions parametrized by the number of zeros of the gauge potential, proved analytically.
